hints: Resolve perpendicular to the $18^\circ$ inclined plane: $R + T\sin 26^\circ - 8g\cos 18^\circ = 0$, so $R = 80\cos 18^\circ - T\sin 26^\circ$.
Since the block accelerates up the plane, friction acts down the plane: $F = \mu R = 0.65 R$.
Resolve parallel to the plane: $T\cos 26^\circ - 8g\sin 18^\circ - F = 8(0.2)$, substitute the expression for $R$, and solve for $T$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R + T\sin 26^\circ - 8g\cos 18^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 80\cos 18^\circ - T\sin 26^\circ \approx 76.0845 - 0.438371 T$$

Express friction $F$ using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.65$:
$$F = 0.65(80\cos 18^\circ - T\sin 26^\circ) = 52\cos 18^\circ - 0.65T\sin 26^\circ$$

Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane with acceleration $a = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ up the slope:
$$T\cos 26^\circ - 8g\sin 18^\circ - F = 8(0.2)$$
$$T\cos 26^\circ - 80\sin 18^\circ - (52\cos 18^\circ - 0.65T\sin 26^\circ) = 1.6$$
$$T(\cos 26^\circ + 0.65\sin 26^\circ) = 1.6 + 80\sin 18^\circ + 52\cos 18^\circ$$

Evaluate the numerical terms and solve for $T$:
$$1.183735 T = 75.7763 \implies T = \frac{75.7763}{1.183735} \approx 64.0\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify all forces acting on the $8\text{ kg}$ block on the plane inclined at $18^\circ$:
- Weight: $W = mg = (8)(10) = 80\text{ N}$ vertically downwards
- Normal reaction: $R$ perpendicular to the plane
- Tension: $T$ in the string at an angle of $26^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope
- Friction: $F$ acting down the plane, since the block accelerates up the plane with $a = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane (taking upward normal as positive):
$$\sum F_{\perp} = 0$$
$$R + T\sin 26^\circ - mg\cos 18^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 80\cos 18^\circ - T\sin 26^\circ$$
Calculate the trigonometric coefficients:
$$80\cos 18^\circ \approx 80(0.951057) = 76.0845\text{ N}$$
$$\sin 26^\circ \approx 0.438371$$
$$R = 76.0845 - 0.438371 T \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Calculate the kinetic friction force $F$ using $F = \mu R$ with $\mu = 0.65$:
$$F = 0.65(76.0845 - 0.438371 T)$$
$$0.65 \times 76.0845 \approx 49.4549\text{ N}$$
$$0.65 \times 0.438371 \approx 0.284941$$
$$F = 49.4549 - 0.284941 T \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the line of greatest slope (taking uphill as positive):
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = ma$$
$$T\cos 26^\circ - mg\sin 18^\circ - F = ma$$
Substitute $mg\sin 18^\circ = 80\sin 18^\circ \approx 80(0.309017) = 24.7214\text{ N}$ and $ma = 8(0.2) = 1.6\text{ N}$:
$$T\cos 26^\circ - 24.7214 - (49.4549 - 0.284941 T) = 1.6$$
Combine the terms in $T$ and the constant terms:
$$\cos 26^\circ \approx 0.898794$$
$$(\cos 26^\circ + 0.284941) T - (24.7214 + 49.4549) = 1.6$$
$$(0.898794 + 0.284941) T - 74.1763 = 1.6$$
$$1.183735 T = 74.1763 + 1.6 = 75.7763$$

Solve for the tension $T$:
$$T = \frac{75.7763}{1.183735} \approx 64.015\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 64.0\text{ N}$.

hints: The fourth second of motion is the time interval from $t = 3\text{ s}$ to $t = 4\text{ s}$.
Use the displacement formula $s(t) = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ from rest with constant acceleration $a = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$s(4) = \frac{1}{2}(0.2)(4^2) = 0.1(16) = 1.6\text{ m}$$

Calculate the displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$s(3) = \frac{1}{2}(0.2)(3^2) = 0.1(9) = 0.9\text{ m}$$

Subtract $s(3)$ from $s(4)$ to find the distance travelled during the fourth second:
$$\text{Distance} = s(4) - s(3) = 1.6 - 0.9 = 0.7\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Understand the phrasing 'distance travelled during the fourth second of motion':
- The 1st second covers $t = 0$ to $t = 1$.
- The 2nd second covers $t = 1$ to $t = 2$.
- The 3rd second covers $t = 2$ to $t = 3$.
- The 4th second covers the time interval from $t = 3\text{ s}$ to $t = 4\text{ s}$.

Use the constant-acceleration displacement equation from rest ($u = 0$):
$$s(t) = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
Substitute $a = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s(t) = \frac{1}{2}(0.2)t^2 = 0.1t^2$$

Calculate the difference:
$$\Delta s = s(4) - s(3) = 1.6 - 0.9 = 0.7\text{ m}$$
Thus, the distance travelled during the fourth second is $0.7\text{ m}$.
